pageCache.text:
Breakfast and Afterschool Clubs
We run a very successful Breakfast Club and After School club which means that we can offer wrap around quality child care where it is needed from 07.45 am to 06.00 pm.
To book regular or adhoc spaces in either the Breakfast or After School Club, please complete and return the bookings form/s below to the school office or via email to admin@marist.surrey.sch.uk. If less than 24 hours notice, please call the School Office on 01932 344477 between 9.30am and 3pm.
If you need to contact the Breakfast or After School Club staff out of school hours, please call the main school office number (01932 344477) and select ‘Extended Schools’ (option 6).
Breakfast Club
Open from 07.45 every morning of term (apart from INSET days), the Breakfast Club is run by our own support staff and offers a filling breakfast and plenty of activities to set your child up for the day at school.
After School Club
Open from the end of the school day to 6.00pm every day of term (apart from INSET days and the last day of term when school closes at 1.15pm), the After School Club offers a happy and relaxed place to relax at the end of the school day. We try to make it more like home than school and offer a wide variety of activities available to all both inside and out. There are a variety of snacks and it’s lots of fun! The Afterschool Club will now include a hot snack with no extra cost.
Please note that at 6:01pm, late charges will apply per child. Please see Appendix A. section 8 - Drop off and Collections of the Breakfast and After School Club Policy.

PE and Sport Premium
Sports Premium
“Leaders make good use of the primary school sports funding to give pupils experience of expert coaching in a range of sports, and to develop teachers’ understanding of how to provide high-quality physical education lessons. As a result, there is now a strong framework for planning these lessons and a helpful emphasis on learning about sports and physical health. This means pupils are enthusiastic about being healthy and taking part in competitive sports.”
The PE and sport premium is an annual dedicated payment for primary schools provided by the Department for Education (DfE) from September 2013. Schools have the discretion to spend the funding as they see fit to improve the quality of PE and sports.
At The Marist, a proportion of our sport funding is used as part payment towards the cost of two level 2 qualified coaches to work with children from Year R to Year 6 developing and applying a variety of physical skills and challenges.

Prayer and Worship
As a Catholic school, prayer and worship lie at the heart of our daily life and routines. Our daily worship and liturgies provide an opportunity for children to develop socially, morally and spiritually. Our children engage in a range of worship forms including celebration, singing, formal, informal and shared. Our children are familiar with the language, silence and stillness of worship. Prayer and worship are shared experiences which are led by staff and children to a high quality.

Religious Education
At The Marist our primary intent in teaching Religious Education is to learn, love and achieve together. We want our children to develop knowledge, understanding, reflection skills, analysis and religious experiences. In our Catholic community, we intend for our children to gain a wide range of experiences to build their sense of belonging alongside their individual faith.
We aims to enable the children to be active participants in RE through our curriculum as well as our whole school worships, Masses and celebrations. These all allow our children to feel they are an important part of our school community.
In line with the stipulation of the Bishop's Conference of England and Wales, the school spends 10% of the teaching week on Religious Education.

With Christ as our guide, we learn, we love, we achieve together.
Welcome to The Marist Catholic Primary School website
Located in the heart of West Byfleet, The Marist is a nurturing two-form entry institution, dedicated to educating children aged 4-11. Our rich heritage of serving the local parish of Our Lady Help of Christians is a testament to our commitment to Catholic values, instilling love and respect for others through the teachings of Christ. Our mission is clear: With Christ as our guide, we learn, we love, we achieve together.
As you explore the pages of our website, you will discover a wealth of information about our school's ethos, curriculum, and community. Every member of Team Marist strives to provide the very best for all of our children, helping them to excel academically, spiritually and emotionally.
Emily Fanzo Head of School
We are proud to offer a well-rounded education that not only equips our children with the skills they need but also instils in them the values of compassion, respect, and service. Our strong ties to the community, and exceptional facilities all contribute to our children becoming the best 'Marist Learners' they can be during their time with us.
